core_obligations: Reduce to the filtered case: arguing as in the dual case, one may assume there are invertible modules and filtrations of the two locally free modules whose successive quotients are those invertible modules (proof lines 8587-8602).

Filter the tensor product: ordering the pairs of indices lexicographically presents the tensor product as a successive extension of the tensor products of the invertible pieces, so that the total Chern class of the tensor product is the product of the corresponding linear factors (proof lines 8603-8621).

Conclude by the product formulas: the three total Chern classes are then the products over the linear factors of the two modules and over the sums of the two families, and the displayed formulas for the first and second Chern classes, and the rest, follow by expanding those products; the author states that this formal computation is omitted (proof lines 8622-8632).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to invertible successive quotients by the same argument as in the dual case (proof lines 8587-8602).
Produce the lexicographic filtration of the tensor product (proof lines 8603-8621).
Read the formulas off the three products of linear factors (proof lines 8622-8632).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Chern classes of the tensor product of two finite locally free modules of ranks r and s, giving in particular the formulas for the first and second Chern classes as linear combinations of the Chern classes of the factors with binomial coefficients (statement lines 8566-8585, tag 0FA6). The proof reduces to the case where both modules are successive extensions of invertible modules by the same argument as in the dual case, constructs the lexicographic filtration of the tensor product whose successive quotients are the tensor products of the invertible pieces, and thereby writes all three total Chern classes as products of linear factors, from which the displayed formulas follow by expansion. The construction of the filtration is the substance, so the claim is H2.
